root_cause.text: The function `skb_try_coalesce()` copies paged fragments from the source `skb` to the destination `skb` but fails to propagate the `SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG` flag, causing `skb_has_shared_frag()` to return false on the destination and allowing in-place decryption (e.g., in ESP) over externally-owned or page-cache-backed pages without proper copying.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `to_shinfo->flags |= from_shinfo->flags & SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG;` when `from_shinfo->nr_frags` is non-zero. The commit message explicitly states: "If @from has SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG set, the resulting @to skb can contain the same externally-owned or page-cache-backed frags, but the shared-frag marker is currently lost." It further describes the security impact: "ESP input checks skb_has_shared_frag() before deciding whether an uncloned nonlinear skb can skip skb_cow_data(). If TCP receive coalescing has moved shared frags into an unmarked skb, ESP can see skb_has_shared_frag() as false and decrypt in place over page-cache backed frags."

This is the size argument for copying frags. It indicates that all source frags are being copied verbatim, including any shared page frags, without transferring the flag that marks them as shared.
This increments the destination frag count by the source count. It is part of the coalescing logic that should also set SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG if any of the added frags are shared, but does not.

This condition checks if the source skb is not cloned. When true, the source's frags are being stolen; the destination takes ownership but still lacks the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag, which is especially dangerous for external pages.
